subject: math

objective.text: Measure with an inch tile by laying one unit end to end with no gaps.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective

explanations.title: Mark and move forward
explanations.text: Put the unit at the start of the line. Mark where it ends. Move the unit forward so its edge sits on the mark. Keep going until the whole line is measured.

source_ref.section: Concept Development

explanations.title: No gaps
explanations.text: Do not leave any space between the units. Use the same size unit every time. The spaces between the hash marks are all the same length.

source_ref.section: Concept Development

explanations.title: The inch tile
explanations.text: An inch tile is a length unit called an inch. It is bigger than a centimeter cube. You can use it the same way as a centimeter cube.

source_ref.section: Concept Development

explanations.title: About how long
explanations.text: A line may not be an exact number of tiles. If it is half a tile longer or more, say about the next number. If it is less than half a tile longer, say about the number you counted.

source_ref.section: Concept Development

explanations.title: Big units and small units
explanations.text: A larger unit covers a length faster. You use fewer of them. A smaller unit takes more moves. Always use the same size unit to compare two lengths.

source_ref.section: Concept Development; Student Debrief

explanations.title: Count units, not marks
explanations.text: Count the length units between the marks. Do not count the hash marks. A line with 5 marks has 4 units between them.

source_ref.section: Student Debrief (counted hash marks instead of length units)

examples.title: Frances and the bookcase
examples.text: Frances uses a book to measure. The bookcase is 5 books long. The space is 4 books long. The bookcase will not fit.

source_ref.section: Concept Development

examples.title: A 4 inch tile line
examples.text: A line has a hash mark at each end. The tile is moved forward 4 times. The spaces between the marks are all the same length. The line is 4 inch tiles long.

The line length matches the stimulus

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.

Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
